scope: Full LLVM native 8/16/32-bit DIV/IDIV intrinsics in protected code16 using the 32-bit stack ABI; code32 and current i386/x64/NeverC regressions. This does not enable an i386 frontend in NeverC.
source_basis: Recorded base commits plus llvm-tested.patch and neverc-tested.patch, with changed/shared input files also retained beneath source-snapshot. Documentation was added after the native runs; compiler and fixture sources remained identical.
count_definition: Each profile counts actual executions, not unique inputs. Protected pairs compare GPRs, flags, system registers/caches, event state and all guest RAM against independent original bytes; #DE frames authenticate their respective restart PCs before normalization. User-mode regressions use the existing SIGFPE/result oracle and are not complete-state pairs.
negative_controls: Erased unused-result DIV is rejected by original-opcode authentication in all six protected compiler profiles.
Zero divisor substituted before an intact DIV is rejected by the declared-input transport check in all six protected profiles.

boundary: Native protected coverage is CPL0 with flat, present page mappings. It proves register division, native #DE delivery, result-use combinations, stack balance and callee-saved registers. It does not qualify memory-divisor faults, other privilege levels or asynchronous events.

The source wrappers use only integer registers; x87/SSE/AVX state is outside this comparison. Flags are native CPU outputs, not a compiler intrinsic return value. The 64-bit pair remains long-mode-only.

The full LLVM fork and NeverC retain their separate target admission. NeverC exposes the native C23 builtins on its existing x64 target; this change adds protected-mode LLVM qualification rather than an i386 frontend.

No production SDK or LLVM gitlink changed. General i386 source dispatch, unlisted state/instructions, real/VM86/tasks, debug, software SMM/SGX and complete CET/FRED event contracts remain open; final release/pin waits for global completion.
